summary: ʔty III mamtele/mamte duplicates mty III, including the twelve-mule quotation.
rationale: Permitted lookup confirms identical paradigm and 57/164 material. Editorial consolidation is required; do not delete mty I, whose mtele/mote reanalysis is distinct.

summary: Keep lazəm mamtát-way-le aʕmux as III Infectum-wa, and treat izúx, mtiy-e l-arke as a cross-reference to mty I Imperativ.
rationale: The compound quotation contains two different formal paradigms. mty I already lists mtiy-e at 51/38; do not create an ʔty III Imperativ from that clause.

summary: New box ko-Preterit: example for sense 1 in ko-Preterit (52/179)

data.turoyo: Komamtelilux i qəṣṣa du ḥadodo d Marde.
data.translation: Ich habe dir die Geschichte des Schmiedes von Mardin gebracht!

rationale: First ko-Preterit box; k(o)- plus mamte-li-lux contains the Preterit agent and recipient indexes. Abstract narrative as theme.

data.turoyo: Hul d ǧbir u greʕo w kəzze, gowe w mamte muklo lu ʕmiro.
data.translation: bis schließlich der Diener betteln gehen mußte, um dem Emir essen zu verschaffen.

rationale: Thin III.1 Infectum cell; food theme and explicit l-recipient.

data.turoyo: Ayna mənxu gəmḏ̣aḥe b nafše d ruḥe, gəzze, mamteli u darmonano?
data.translation: Welcher von euch will sich opfern und gehen und mir das Heilmittel herbringen?

rationale: Thin III.1 Infectum cell; medicinal theme and first-person recipient.

data.turoyo: U zlamano ṭr oṯe l flan utel, falge d yawmo kobaʕnole, i saʕa traḥṣar, kətli səsyo, d mamtele lu xan!
data.translation: Dieser Mann soll heute Mittag um zwölf Uhr in das und das Gasthaus kommen. Ich habe ein Pferd, das soll er in die Herberge bringen!

rationale: Thin III.1 Infectum cell; mamte-le is an Infectum with a patient suffix, not automatically a Preterit.

data.turoyo: Qayəm, azzano, u ahl di qriṯo, b hawari, ḥatta d ḥozinanne w d mamtina laǧ ǧanazataṯṯe.
data.translation: wir, die Leute des Dorfes, machten uns auf zu einer Hilfsexpedition, um sie zu finden und ihre Leichen zu holen.

rationale: Fills III.1 Infectum to five; l-marked corpse themes in a purpose clause.

summary: New idiom: mamtele/mamte admo m- 'Blut vergießen'

data.turoyo: Uṣḥa d mamtutu admo mu zlamano, mamtutəlle saġ larke!
data.translation: Hütet euch, das Blut diese Mannes zu vergießen! Ihr sollt ihn lebendig hierher bringen.

rationale: Light verb plus blood noun, contrasted with literal bringing in the same sentence. No matching collocation found in permitted lookup or the related mṭy 1 idiom list.

summary: Exact mamte spellings are retained under ʔty III following the inherited 57/67 example. Permitted lookups confirm duplication with mty III and a related but differently spelled emphatic mṭy 1 III; no automatic root merger is justified.

The ko-Preterit Komamtelilux carries both agent -li and recipient -lux and supplies a missing box. It is not merely an Infectum with ko-. By contrast d mamtele at 57/127 has a theme suffix in a dependent prospective clause.
Theme marking includes zero nominal objects, pronominal objects and l-marked corpse objects; recipients can be independent l- phrases or suffixes, and l- also marks a destination such as the inn.
The blood collocation is a light-verb construction, already embedded in the inherited 57/67 quotation. Literal bringing a man alive immediately follows it; the two uses must be analysed separately.
The mtiy-e instruction in the inherited Infectum-wa quotation belongs to the independently reanalysed mty I paradigm, which remains distinct from duplicated mty III.
Choose a canonical entry for the duplicated ʔty III/mty III mamtele paradigm while retaining mty I and separately examining ʔṯy III mayte and mṭy 1 III mamṭe.
Confirm the segmentation of mamtəlla at 57/30 before using that form as paradigm evidence.
Does mamte admo m- cover any drawing of blood, or specifically violent bloodshed? The example forbids bloodshed and requires the man alive; do not infer killing as the sole meaning.
A story is an abstract transported theme; food, medicine, horses, people and corpses preserve the same bring construction.
